regime.headline: Risk-OFF, on 2 of 3 independent pairs. Consumer Appetite and Equity Beta Appetite are favouring the defensive leg. Treat long setups as counter-trend and demand better evidence for them.

metrics.label: Credit Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: The quarter (+3.4pp) and the month (+2.3pp) point the same way, so the read is not resting on one window.
metrics.explanation: HYG has outperformed TLT by 3.4pp over the quarter — risk-ON.
metrics.whyItMatters: High-yield credit against long Treasuries. Both are duration-sensitive, so the rate move cancels and what is left is whether investors are being paid to take default risk and taking it.
metrics.nextTrigger: flips when HYG stops outperforming TLT over a quarter

metrics.label: Consumer Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: The quarter (-1.6pp) and the month (-0.3pp) point the same way, so the read is not resting on one window.
metrics.explanation: XLY has underperformed XLP by 1.6pp over the quarter — risk-OFF.
metrics.whyItMatters: Discretionary against staples. Both are the same consumer in the same economy; the ratio is whether that consumer is buying optional things, which turns before earnings do.
metrics.nextTrigger: flips when XLY stops underperforming XLP over a quarter

metrics.label: Equity Beta Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: The quarter (-0.7pp) and the month (-5.3pp) point the same way, so the read is not resting on one window.
metrics.explanation: SMH has underperformed SPY by 0.7pp over the quarter — risk-OFF.
metrics.whyItMatters: Semiconductors against the index. Semis are the highest-beta liquid expression of the equity market, so this measures willingness to hold the volatile end rather than equities in general.
metrics.nextTrigger: flips when SMH stops underperforming SPY over a quarter

rotationNarrative: 11.2 points separate the best and worst sector over the last month, so which sector you own is doing real work. Energy leads on both horizons (+4.4pp vs SPY over a month). Capital is rotating INTO Health Care, Materials, Financials, Industrials — behind over six months, ahead over one. It is rotating OUT of Semiconductors, which still look strong on the six-month number and are not.
